summary: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no source found describes the tower itself.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no source describes what remains.

evidence.supports: FFLA lists a Lindale tower in Smith County at 32.54598, -95.36681
FFLA marks the Lindale tower as gone
Community of the same name lies on the Missouri Pacific Railroad and U.S. Highway 69, ten miles north of Tyler in northwestern Smith County
evidence.quote: Lindale is on the Missouri Pacific Railroad and U.S. Highway 69 ten miles north of Tyler in northwestern Smith County.

evidence.supports: Townsite settled as early as 1873 when a post office opened under the name Lyndale
evidence.quote: The site, originally part of the Thomas Burbridge survey, was settled as early as 1873, when the Lyndale post office opened with John M. Davis as postmaster.

evidence.supports: Spelling changed to Lindale the next year; in 1875 the settlement became a station on the International-Great Northern Railroad
evidence.quote: The next year the spelling was changed to Lindale, and in 1875 the settlement became a station on the new International-Great Northern Railroad.

sources.title: Texas Lookouts, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Thin. The only tower-specific source is the FFLA Texas list, which gives name, county, coordinates and gone status and nothing else. Not on NHLR or FFLOS. Two searches and a handful of page reads found no build date, design, staffing, fires or site description. Recent Lindale fire coverage from 2026 was seen in search results but is about a different event and was not used. The TSHA material describes the town, not the tower; the link between the tower and the community rests on the shared name, which no source states. Coordinates were not checked against a map. The editor may cut the community paragraph if it reads as padding.
